prerequisites: Basic knowledge of materials science as taught in the course "Introduction to Materials Science" (H01D0A).

learning_outcomes.text: Students acquire the necessary knowledge and skills regarding the sustainability and circularity of materials and their applications.
The student can place technological knowledge of materials and material processing in a broader sustainability context and knows a number of frameworks for describing material sustainability.

The student has knowledge of various methods to measure ecological, economic, and social aspects of sustainability in an engineering context, and is able to critically interpret results of such measurement methods.
At the end of the course, the student is able to perform a simplified analysis of the environmental impact of products.
The student can make a responsible material choice based on the sustainability of the material's application.
The student has assimilated the principles of circular economy and the possible ways to achieve them.
The student understands why some specific material families and material processing techniques are more circular than others and has knowledge of the properties of those circular materials.

As engineers, students can think systemically: when the themes discussed in this and other courses are addressed, they spontaneously look for coherence with other themes and weigh statements or positions against the broader framework, with attention to sustainability.

Students have developed the reflex to critically approach statements regarding raw material supply, sustainability, and circularity of materials and verify them using recent information and insights, quantitatively if necessary.

syllabus_topics: Sustainability frameworks and sustainable development goals
Measuring and goals of sustainability in an engineering context
Life cycle (analysis) and eco-audit of materials
Social sustainability of materials (extraction, production and waste)
Multi-criteria analyses and system dynamic modeling
Exercises on eco-audit, including process tree, functional unit, CO2 footprint
Exercises on interpretation of sustainability evaluations - Discussion/Pitching/Question session
Group presentation assignment on material selection in a sustainable context
assessment_rules: The final result is a weighted score: 20% from the group paper and 80% from the final exam. If a student does not participate in the scheduled group presentation or one of the two partial evaluations, the final assessment for the course will be 'NA' (not taken). For the second examination opportunity, the evaluation characteristics and determination of the final result are identical to the first opportunity. The score obtained on the group presentation from the first opportunity is recounted for the second opportunity.
institution: KU Leuven - Faculty of Engineering Science
degree: Bachelor in de ingenieurswetenschappen (Bachelor of Engineering Science, Leuven)
